newsitem.title: USA: FBI chief pleased with Saudi efforts on bombing.
newsitem.headline: FBI chief pleased with Saudi efforts on bombing.

text.p: The FBI said on Sunday it was pleased with Saudi efforts to investigate the truck bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen on June 25.
In a statement issued following a visit to Saudi Arabia by FBI Director Louis Freeh, the bureau said close cooperation between the FBI and Saudi authorities would continue.
Freeh was "pleased with the efforts and thoroughness of the Saudi law enforcement authorities to solve this heinous act of terrorism," the FBI statement said.
The visit was arranged at the invitation of the Saudi government and was the third trip by Freeh to Saudi Arabia since the bombing.

FBI officials previously complained about a lack of Saudi cooperation in the investigation of the bombing at the U.S. military housing complex in Dhahran. They said FBI agents were not allowed to question Saudi citizens and were not told about any arrests.
Defense Secretary William Perry told reporters on Nov. 1 the United States had not concluded who was responsible for the bombing. He was scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia next weekend.
National Security Adviser Anthony Lake said Freeh's talks with the Saudis were very successful.
"It's part of a continuing effort with the Saudis to find who was responsible for this terrible act," Lake said on NBC Television's "Meet the Press" program.
